rendering_both_cuts: Build the timeline once. The narration track and the explanatory-label layer are the only two things that swap. Lock picture before either VO is recorded — if a frame changes after recording, both languages must be re-timed and the two cuts will drift.

language_layers.layer: On-screen **explanatory** labels ("rows surviving", "this is the bug")

captions_accessibility: Two `.vtt` files — `en.vtt` and `ar-EG.vtt` — aligned to the same timeline.
Burned-in Egyptian-Arabic captions on the Arabic cut, RTL, bottom, with a 60 %-opacity plate behind them so they survive a busy diagram.
Latin technical terms inside Arabic captions stay LTR — wrap them so bidirectional rendering does not reverse `SELECT *` or `p95`.

Every scene has a text equivalent of its current state, e.g. "INNER JOIN, step 3 of 6. Four of five left rows match." This is also the audio-description script and the alt text for any still exported from the film.
Reduced-motion cut: a version where each scene holds its meaningful first and final frame. Narration unchanged. This doubles as the slide deck.
Contrast: 4.5 : 1 text, 3 : 1 meaningful non-text marks, verified with the real relative-luminance formula, not by eye.
Never encode meaning in colour alone — pair every colour with a shape, a label or a position. The four break classes in CH-28 carry icons as well as colours.
No essential label below 22 px at 1080p.
Chapter markers in the container so a viewer can jump directly to a domain.

content: Every chapter in §7 exists in §8 with both narration tracks written.
Every topic in §12.1 appears in at least one chapter.
Every number on screen traces to §6. No exceptions.
Every chapter declares at least one pattern from §2.
Every chapter has a failure beat, a callback and a named artifact.
At least one prediction prompt per act.
visual: No static bullet list anywhere a pattern was specified.
Every arrow carries a moving mark, or has been deleted.
Every metric that moves has its cause in the same frame.
Only the six permitted 3D scenes are 3D, each with a written justification.
Asset A-01 appears at the end of every act and is identical each time.
Every scene has a meaningful first frame and a meaningful final frame.
language: No code, command, identifier, table name, product name, acronym or number translated.
Every glossed term in §10.1 is glossed on first appearance only.
Latin terms inside Arabic captions render LTR and are not reversed.
The Arabic register is natural Egyptian — no heavy MSA, no exaggerated slang.
technical: English and Arabic cuts have identical frame counts and chapter boundaries.
Audio at −16 LUFS, true peak ≤ −1 dBTP; ambient bed at −30 LUFS.
Both `.vtt` files align to the timeline; Arabic captions burned in on the Arabic cut.
Contrast measured, not estimated: 4.5 : 1 text, 3 : 1 meaningful non-text.
No essential label below 22 px at 1080p.
Chapter markers present in the container.
honesty: CH-02 states once that the simulations are teaching models, not live systems.
CH-35's completion-versus-proof distinction is not undercut by a certificate end card.
The "Carbon database" ambiguity is named in CH-23, not merged away.
Version-sensitive claims live in an end card with a verification date, not in narration.

honest_limits: Nothing in this film was executed during its writing. The numbers in §6 are carried from the working labs in the sources, which computed rather than asserted them. If a figure is re-derived during production and differs, update §6 and re-render rather than quietly using a different number in one cut.
The visual simulations teach the shape of real output. They are not connected to a real database, cluster, cloud account or model. Say so on screen once, in CH-02, and never again.

"Carbon database" remains ambiguous in the underlying job context — Apache CarbonData (a columnar format on HDFS queried through Spark SQL) and GaussDB/openGauss (a PostgreSQL-family RDBMS) are different products. CH-23 teaches the transferable core — columnar layout, sort columns, segments and compaction, partition pruning, predicate pushdown, plan reading — which is correct for either, and names the ambiguity rather than merging them.

Version-sensitive claims (which release is current, which feature exists) are deliberately absent from the narration. Put them in an end card with a verification date, because they go stale and narration cannot be patched.
Completion is not proof. The film says this in CH-35 and the production must not undercut it with a certificate at the end.
